newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner to win Jotun contract - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner to win Jotun contract - newspaper.

text.p: Norwegian group Kvaerner ASA stands to win a production ship contract worth two billion crowns for Esso Norge's Jotun field in the North Sea, the Norwegian newspaper Stavanger Aftenblad said on Tuesday.
A Kvaerner spokesman declined comment on the report.
"We don't comment on market rumours," the spokesman said.
Stavanger Aftenblad said Esso would award the contract for the Floating Production, Storage and Offloading (FPSO) vessel next week to Kvaerner Rosenberg.
"The hull will be built at Kvaerner Masa in Finland, while a lot of the equipment will be installed at Rosenberg shipyard," the unsourced report said.
The newspaper said ABB Offshore Technology was favoured to win the contract to build the 1.7 billion crown wellhead platform for the development.
"If so, it would mean that the fabrication will be carried out at Dutch-Norwegian Heerema in Toensberg," it said.
Esso submitted a plan for development and operation for the oilfield to the Norwegian Energy Ministry in January.
